subject: Geography
description: Covers Karewas, Palk Strait, Nilgiris, and Majuli.

questions.stem: In the context of the Indian subcontinent's physiography, what is the 'Karewa' formation in Kashmir famous for cultivating?

options.option_text: Saffron (Zaffran)
Tea
Coffee
Apples

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Karewas' are thick deposits of glacial clay and other materials embedded with moraines found in the Kashmir Valley. They were formed during the Pleistocene epoch when the valley was a massive lake. Today, these elevated, flat-topped terraces are exceptionally fertile and are world-renowned for the cultivation of high-quality Saffron (Zaffran), as well as almonds and walnuts.
DECOY BUSTING: Tea requires well-drained acidic soils (Assam, Darjeeling). Coffee requires laterite soils and shade (Karnataka, Kerala). Apples are grown in Kashmir, but the Karewa soils specifically are famous for Saffron.
EXAM INSIGHT: Kashmiri Saffron received the prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2020. The Pampore region is the hub of this cultivation.

questions.stem: Which narrow body of water separates the Indian mainland (Tamil Nadu) from the island nation of Sri Lanka?

options.option_text: Palk Strait
Ten Degree Channel
Gulf of Khambhat
Strait of Malacca

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Palk Strait is the narrow, shallow strait between the southeastern coast of India (Tamil Nadu) and the northern coast of Sri Lanka (Jaffna Peninsula). It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with Palk Bay in the southwest.
DECOY BUSTING: 
- The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.
- The Gulf of Khambhat is on the west coast of India (Gujarat).
- The Strait of Malacca separates the Malay Peninsula from the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
EXAM INSIGHT: The strait is named after Robert Palk, a British Governor of the Madras Presidency. The chain of limestone shoals stretching across this strait is known as Adam's Bridge or Ram Setu.

questions.stem: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at which mountain range in southern India?

options.option_text: Nilgiri Hills
Cardamom Hills
Anaimalai Hills
Vindhya Range

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Nilgiri Hills (Blue Mountains) form the majestic junction where the discontinuous Eastern Ghats meet the continuous Western Ghats. They are located at the tri-junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. 
DECOY BUSTING: The Anaimalai and Cardamom Hills are located further south of the Nilgiris (part of the Western Ghats). The Vindhyas divide North and South India.
EXAM INSIGHT: Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills. The region is famous for the Nilgiri Mountain Railway (a toy train that uses a unique rack and pinion system) and the Toda indigenous tribe.

questions.stem: Majuli, recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records as the world's largest river island, is located on which river?

options.option_text: Brahmaputra
Ganga
Godavari
Mahanadi

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Majuli is a massive, incredibly fertile river island nestled in the Brahmaputra River in Assam. It was formed due to course changes by the river and its tributaries. It is a hub of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture (Sattras).
DECOY BUSTING: The Ganga forms Sagar Island in its delta. The Godavari forms islands in its delta near Rajahmundry. But Majuli is uniquely Brahmaputra.
EXAM INSIGHT: In 2016, Majuli became the very first island in India to be made a separate district. However, it faces a severe existential threat from massive soil erosion during the annual Brahmaputra floods, rapidly shrinking its landmass.

questions.stem: The Great Indian Desert (Thar Desert), one of the world's most populous arid zones, is predominantly located in which Indian state?

options.option_text: Gujarat, spread across the coastal Rann of Kutch region
Rajasthan, stretching westward from the Aravalli ranges
Haryana, covering the semi-arid belt near Hisar district
Punjab, in the southwestern Firozpur–Fazilka sandy tract

questions.explanation: Over 85% of the Thar Desert lies in Rajasthan, west of the Aravallis which act as a moisture barrier blocking monsoon winds. Gujarat is a common distractor because of the Rann of Kutch, but the Rann is a salt marsh — a physiographically distinct feature, not a sandy desert.

questions.stem: Which narrow sea channel separates the Andaman island group from the Nicobar island group in the Bay of Bengal?

options.option_text: Duncan Passage, between South Andaman and Little Andaman islands
Ten Degree Channel, lying at 10°N latitude between the two groups
Nine Degree Channel, between Minicoy and the main Lakshadweep group
Coco Channel, between India's territory and Myanmar's Coco Islands

questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel at latitude 10°N separates the Andaman Islands (north) from the Nicobar Islands (south). The Duncan Passage is the most common wrong answer — it lies within the Andamans, between South Andaman and Little Andaman, not between the two island groups.

questions.stem: The northeastern Indian hill ranges — Patkai, Naga, Manipur, and Mizo — are collectively classified under which physiographic unit?

options.option_text: Purvanchal ranges, forming the eastern boundary with Myanmar
Vindhyan ranges, marking the northern edge of the Deccan block
Meghalaya Plateau, an eastward extension of the Peninsular block
Arakan ranges, which are their continuation into Myanmar territory

questions.explanation: The Purvanchal ('Eastern Mountains') comprises the Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, and Mizo (Lushai) Hills along India's eastern frontier. Option D (Arakan Yoma) is a plausible distractor — it is the southward continuation of these same ranges, but Arakan lies entirely within Myanmar, not India.

questions.stem: The Palakkad Gap — the widest and lowest break in the Western Ghats — serves as a natural passage between which two states?

options.option_text: Goa and Karnataka, facilitating road traffic along the Sahyadris
Kerala and Tamil Nadu, enabling east-west transit to Coimbatore
Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, where the Brahmagiri hill ranges narrow
Maharashtra and Karnataka, where the Deccan lava plateau begins

questions.explanation: The Palakkad (Palghat) Gap lies in Kerala's Palakkad district and links it to Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. It also allows moist southwest monsoon winds to penetrate deeper into Tamil Nadu, shaping its climate. Karnataka–Tamil Nadu (option C) is a distractor because the Brahmagiri is a separate hill feature near Kodagu, not related to the Palakkad Gap.

questions.stem: In the Himalayan foothill zone, what primary physiographic characteristic distinguishes the Bhabar belt from the Terai belt lying immediately south of it?

options.option_text: Marshy terrain with tall grasses and seasonal inundation cycles
Porous gravelly alluvium where rivers sink and flow underground
Fertile fine alluvial deposits suited for intensive paddy farming
Hard laterite crusts making it unfit for agriculture or habitation

questions.explanation: The Bhabar belt consists of coarse porous gravel and boulders; Himalayan rivers lose their surface flow here by sinking underground. The Terai (option A — marshy, grass-covered) is where these underground streams re-emerge to the south. A common error is reversing the two belts' descriptions.

questions.stem: The flat-floored, fertile longitudinal valleys nestled between the Shivalik (Outer Himalaya) and the Lesser Himalayan ranges are specifically known as?

options.option_text: Duns — structural synclinal valleys like Dehradun and Kotli Dun
Duars — forested alluvial foothill tracts at the Bhutan-Bengal edge
Karewas — elevated lacustrine terraces within the Kashmir Valley
Chos — deeply gullied ravines cut by Shivalik flashflood streams

questions.explanation: Duns (from Sanskrit 'droni', meaning valley) are synclinal depressions between the Shivaliks and the Lesser Himalayas — Dehradun, Patli Dun, and Kotli Dun are textbook examples. 'Duars' (option B) is the most common wrong answer: Duars are the forested foothill tracts bordering Bhutan along Assam/Bengal, a wholly separate physiographic feature with a different formation mechanism.

questions.stem: The Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau is physiographically distinct from all other northeastern hill ranges because it is geologically an extension of which ancient formation?

options.option_text: Tibetan Plateau's southward extension along the Mishmi block
Peninsular Gondwana block, detached by the Brahmaputra rift graben
Himalayan fold ranges uplifted during the Eocene-Oligocene period
Indo-Burman ranges that form the Tertiary fold mountain belt

questions.explanation: The Meghalaya Plateau shares the same Archaean crystalline basement (Gondwana fragment) as the Deccan Plateau, making it part of the ancient Peninsular Block. It became isolated when the Brahmaputra valley graben (rift depression) subsided, separating it from the main plateau. Options C and D describe the Himalayan and Indo-Burman ranges — Tertiary fold mountains of entirely different age and tectonic origin.
